label: prop:mirror-baseline-cancellation
title: Mirror-pair cancellation of the bar-even binding baseline
html:
Proposition. Mirror-pair cancellation of the bar-even binding baseline

Let (Z, N) and (N, Z) be a mirror pair at fixed mass number A = Z + N, with crossing statistics of the atom braid word

\sigma + \sigma^{-1} = 10A - 2, \qquad \mathrm{avg} = 2A + 1, \qquad
w = \sigma - \sigma^{-1} = 4Z .

Then the two bar-even statistics are mirror-invariant, (\sigma+\sigma^{-1})(Z,N) = (\sigma+\sigma^{-1})(N,Z) and \mathrm{avg}(Z,N) = \mathrm{avg}(N,Z), while the writhe is the unique distinguishing statistic,

w(Z,N) - w(N,Z) = 4(Z - N).

Consequently, for any binding-exponent deviation of the additive form f(Z,N) = \beta(A) + \zeta(Z-N) — an A-only baseline \beta plus an interface-imbalance term \zeta — the mirror difference cancels the baseline exactly:

f(Z,N) - f(N,Z) = \zeta(Z-N) - \zeta(N-Z).

The two bar-even crossing invariants depend only on A (the Z, N coefficients cancel in \sigma + \sigma^{-1} and in \mathrm{avg}), so they are identical across a mirror pair; the bar-odd writhe w = 4Z is the sole crossing content that distinguishes the two members. The cancellation of \beta(A) in the mirror difference is therefore unconditional once the deviation is written in the additive form \beta(A) + \zeta(Z-N) — that separation is the only hypothesis, justified by the mirror-invariance of the bar-even statistics and supplied (not derived) as the additive-channel ansatz.

Thus, the observed mirror splits are clean numerical values (\zeta(+1) - \zeta(-1) \approx -1.34 for {}^{3}\mathrm{He}/{}^{3}\mathrm{H}, \approx -1.77 for {}^{7}\mathrm{Be}/{}^{7}\mathrm{Li}) even where absolute deviations are large and A-dependent. This holds even past the A \le 4 regime. The difference isolates the bar-odd Z-correction from the A-dependent baseline. The sign of \zeta is fixed by the per-nucleon intra-\mathcal{B}_3 writhe asymmetry (proton +3 > neutron +1); its magnitude is open and unfitted.
